recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. If PA wants to revisit whether .active should distinguish inactive from entered-in-error or whether active should remain a modifier, handle that as a new cross-resource active/status tracker rather than by reapplying the older DSTU1 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-3847 was a Published / Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 PA issue asking that incorrectly marked isModifier fields be removed from RelatedPerson; its final resolution said all RelatedPerson isModifier fields had been removed.
initial_application: No current git commit in this checkout mentions FHIR-3847, suggesting the original application occurred in older legacy source. The current build no longer has a broad set of RelatedPerson modifier flags; it has exactly one, on RelatedPerson.active.
additional_context: FHIR-10364 later added an active flag and search parameter to RelatedPerson, Schedule, and HealthcareService so those resources could be marked inactive/not in current use, consistent with Patient, Practitioner, and Person. Published STU3, R4, and R5 RelatedPerson definitions and the current source all expose RelatedPerson.active as a modifier because it can indicate that a record should not be treated as valid. FHIR-54873 confirms the same current .active modifier rationale for a parallel resource status pattern.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Removing RelatedPerson.active.isModifier would conflict with later approved active/status semantics and the current published FHIR pattern.

related_jiras.note: Added RelatedPerson.active after the DSTU1 cleanup, consistent with Patient, Practitioner, and Person.
Confirms the current .active modifier rationale for a parallel resource status pattern.
